extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and those following Allied/war-crimes trials
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article describing evidence, procedures, and preliminary plans for the Nuremberg and forthcoming Japanese war-crimes trials, including prosecutorial focus, trial structure, rights of defendants, and types of evidence. It reports on legal/administrative standards the Allies intend to follow in trying large groups of suspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents not used by the prosecution as evidence, since they were not relevant to the argument then under discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only documents relevant to the charges and argument should be admitted; material discovered may be mentioned but excluded from the record when irrelevant to the specific point before the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: “The accused will be presumed innocent until proved guilty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutors and courts must observe the presumption throughout pretrial and trial proceedings; public statements should not undermine this presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and open trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials probably would be free and open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are expected to be accessible to the public and press to ensure transparency; the article states trials 'would be free and open.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel (own or appointed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants may 'prepare for trial either [with] their own counsel, if desired, or appointed counsel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accused must be given opportunity to retain counsel or receive appointed representation so they can prepare a defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair notice of charges
rubrics_metrics.description: “The accused would be given fair notice of charges against them so that they do not think I committed any crimes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges should be formally communicated in sufficient detail and time to enable defendants to understand and prepare a defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expeditious/rapid conclusion of trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that 'trials be concluded as rapidly as possible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities emphasized speedy disposition to avoid prolonged detention and backlog; trial planning includes timetables and grouping strategies to expedite proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of delay-by-technicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to be 'a Roman holiday for technicalities either by the prosecution or defense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should resist frivolous procedural maneuvers that unduly delay or derail substantive adjudication of charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentencing discretion within court charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties would be 'within elastic limits' and be at the option of the court under a court charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentencing is to be determined by the tribunal within prescribed bounds rather than by rigid mandatory penalties; courts have discretion subject to charter rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group (joint) trials structured by time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Japanese war crimes suspects 'will be tried in groups' and groups 'built around four broad time periods... will go back to July, 1937.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To handle large numbers of defendants, trials will be organized into groups (often by era or campaign) rather than individual trials; indictments will cover specified temporal spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: International tribunal / multinational participation
rubrics_metrics.description: “An international court seems likely, since other interested powers have been asked.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribunal composition should include multiple Allied/interested powers to lend legitimacy and share jurisdiction; coordination among nations is expected in nominations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecutorial focus on planners and command-level defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution 'turned most of their evidence against the German military and naval leaders... pointing out their part in plans for the crushing invasion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis will be on prosecuting high-ranking officials and planners responsible for aggressive war and large-scale atrocities rather than only lower-level perpetrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of admissible documentary and testimonial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence introduced included 'captured documents and secret speeches by Hitler,' intelligence reports, directives, naval orders, letters, diaries, and operational plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution intends to rely heavily on captured documentary materials (orders, directives, letters, diaries, intelligence reports) and eyewitness/testimonial evidence to demonstrate intent, planning and execution of crimes; examples provided include naval orders to use enemy flags, Hitler directives, Jodl's diary and intelligence reports about troop camouflaging.
